#### Retrieving your work

This and all future homework .Rmd files are written in Markdown. The .Rmd file can be rendered as an .html file for easier viewing. 

Once you have opened the .Rmd file, you may begin writing your answers beneath each problem. Do not remove any of the original problems from the file, because that makes it more difficult for the me to grade your assignment. 

#### Submitting your work

When you upload your files to Canvas, you are to submit ***two*** files:

a. Your reproducible document file (.Rmd) which should be saved as homework##-ID.Rmd. For example, my homework08 file would be saved as homework09-jperrigan.Rmd.

b. Your rendered reproducible document file (.html) which should be saved as homework##-ID.html. For example, my homework08 file would be saved as homework09-jperrigan.html.

Your ID is your Canvas username. It is also the text before the "@" symbol in your UNO email address.

You have an unlimited number of submissions, but only the  latest submission will be viewed and graded. **Proper means that the file is correctly named and formatted. Latest means that the file is the most recent submission prior to the deadline. Remember the .Rmd file needs to render properly to .html before submitting.**

### Use the URLs to access the data. No local files allowed.


For this problem set, we will be looking at the dataset "econmath", which looks at scores in an Economics class at Michigan State.

$score = \beta_0 + \beta_1 age + \beta_2 work + \beta_3 study + \beta_4 act + \beta_5 male + u$, 

where $score$ is course score in percentage points, $age$ is age in years, $work$ is hours worked per week, $study$ is hours spent studying per week, $act$ is a composite ACT score, and $male = 1$ if male. 

The econmath data is in the wooldridge package. We will omit any rows with missing values by using na.omit().

```{r}
data("econmath")
econmath = na.omit(econmath)
?econmath
```
